overview: Tiwi communities connect kinship, seasonal knowledge and distinctive arts with their island Country. Their cultural identity continues through families, artists and community institutions.

items.text: Yiminga skin groups pass through mothers and organise marriage, obligations, songs and ceremonial relationships. Children learn these connections from an early age.
The seasonal calendar recognises overlapping changes in weather, flowering and animal behaviour. Eucalyptus flowering signals cold dry-season weather; bird calls help anticipate seasonal change.
During hot weather, food gathering concentrates in mangroves and forest patches. The emerald dove's call marks a time associated with Kurlama yams and ceremony.
Artists grind natural ochres and can heat yellow ochre to make red. A wooden comb called pwoja applies fine dot patterns to skin and other surfaces.
Tiwi-owned art centres support work in painting, carving, printmaking and textiles. These media carry cultural stories into contemporary artistic practice.
The Tiwi Land Council was established in 1978 after years of advocacy for recognition of Tiwi custodianship. This institutional date is not the beginning of Tiwi society.
